utterances.text: Can we agree that these are basically two positions?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is that Mahala?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And is it Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But can we agree that Kruscica, down towards the south, through the woods, has an open access?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, if you want to ask things, the value is limited if at all if you ask the questions. You must really allow the witness to give the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I was trying to cut the time but I gave up the question because Kruscica we have heard many things, so it was obviously not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As things are happening, Mr. Kovacic, one has the feeling that you are testifying. You are the one who is testifying, so we shouldn't reverse the parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Roads, there was talk about roads. Let us just make it quite clear, how many roads, main thoroughfares are there through the Lasva Valley around Vitez between Kaonik and Travnik, so roughly speaking east-west?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: There is one main road, and one roundabout but there is one main road, one main highway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The first that you mentioned goes through the town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: It is, it goes through Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the other one you called a roundabout?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: One goes through and that is the main road. That one goes through the fields and another one goes through Mahala, I mean through the town, and then they come together on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And from that point when they come together onward, there is only one road?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the same thing on the east before they branch off, there is one road?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were shown this certificate, I'm referring to Z1473.11. Did you happen to notice the date as the end of your service with the military?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us which date is it here?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: 30th of March, 1996, which is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: At that time, say, in March 1996, what were you doing at the time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly, but I quit the army as soon as the war was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That was roughly when?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO MARJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, 1994, in early 1994 when the conflict ended, when the cease-fire was signed, I stopped being active.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Marjanovic, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, while the witness is going, but bearing in mind the five minutes that we had, is this a matter which you could deal with in a minute or would you prefer between witnesses tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It will take about four or five minutes to set the position out, I think. It doesn't require, I think, a response. I'm really acting, at the moment, to provide information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could do it tomorrow morning between witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes we'll adjourn now until tomorrow morning, half past nine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
